faq: Which platforms can you move from?

WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, Magento, BigCommerce, PrestaShop and most others that can export a CSV file or have an API. Tell us the platform in the order form and we confirm it can be moved before we start.
Will my old links and rankings survive?
We map old addresses to new Shopify pages with 301 redirects, which tell search engines where each page moved. Rankings can still dip for a while after any move, so we do not promise how it will go.
Can you move past orders and customer passwords?
Orders and customer records can come across with an import app, which you pay for directly. Passwords cannot be moved, so customers are invited to set a new one. We explain this before you switch.
What happens to my old store?

It stays online and untouched while we work. Only after you approve the new store do we connect your domain to Shopify. Cancelling the old platform plan is up to you, and we advise waiting until things are stable.
desc:
Migrate to Shopify from any platform without losing products, customers or search visibility. Ecom Swift LLC moves your store from WooCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, Magento, BigCommerce and more into your own Shopify account, with 301 redirects mapped for every old page.

## What does it mean to migrate to Shopify?

A Shopify migration is the transfer of your store's data and web addresses from your current platform to a new Shopify store. The data includes products, variants, images, collections, customers, blog posts and, where possible, past orders. The addresses matter just as much, because they decide whether old links and search results still work.

Moving a store is a careful rebuild of its data and not a simple file transfer. Each platform stores data differently, so fields must be exported, cleaned, matched to Shopify's structure and imported in the right order. Done carefully, shoppers notice a faster, simpler store and not a disruption.

## Why moving matters and why it goes wrong

Owners usually move because their current platform has become costly, slow, limited or hard to manage. Shopify offers a hosted store with built-in checkout and a large app ecosystem, which suits many growing sellers.

The risk lies in the details. Missing images, broken variants, lost customer records and old links that lead to error pages can cost traffic and trust. Search engines have spent time learning your old addresses, and if those addresses simply vanish, the pages that earned visitors disappear with them.

## How a careful move protects traffic

Search visibility depends on pages that already exist in the index. A 301 redirect tells browsers and search engines that a page has moved permanently and where to find it. When every old address points to its new equivalent, shoppers with bookmarks and visitors from search land on the right product instead of a dead end.

We cannot promise that rankings stay identical, because a change of platform also changes page speed, structure and content details. What we can do is remove the avoidable causes of loss: missing redirects, lost titles and descriptions, and gaps in the catalog.

## What a complete migration includes

- Products with titles, descriptions, prices, SKUs and images imported correctly.
- Variants, options and inventory mapped to Shopify's structure.
- Collections and categories rebuilt so shoppers can browse as before.
- Customers imported with their addresses.
- Past orders imported for your records on higher packages.
- Blog posts and key pages moved.
- A redirect map from every important old web address to its new one.
- Theme set up with your logo and colors, plus payments, shipping and tax settings.
- Customer feedback content moved where your old platform allows it to be exported.
- A switch-over plan and domain connection, so the change happens at a time you choose.

## How we do the migration

We start by exporting your data from the old store and inspecting it. We clean up duplicates, missing images and inconsistent names before anything is imported. Then we import products, collections and customers into your Shopify account and check samples against the old store.

Next we build the redirect list by comparing old and new addresses, and we test it. Your old store stays online while we work, so nothing is interrupted. When you approve the new store, we plan the switch-over, connect your domain and check the redirects again. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in catalog size, how many pages are redirected and whether customers, orders and the switch-over plan are included. Customer passwords cannot be copied between platforms, so customers set a new one when they first log in.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your old store active until the new one is checked.
- Export a backup of your data before we begin.
- Decide which products and pages you no longer need before the move.
- Test checkout with a real order before switching your domain.
- Tell us about any special URLs, such as campaign or landing pages.

**Avoid:**
- Switching the domain before redirects are in place.
- Importing messy product data and hoping to tidy it later.
- Changing product names and page addresses at the same time as the move.
- Cancelling the old platform before you confirm everything transferred.
- Forgetting to update links in emails, ads and social profiles.

## Who this is for

This service suits sellers outgrowing WooCommerce or Wix, businesses on a platform they find hard to maintain, and owners who inherited a store on a system they do not know. It also suits merchants with a large catalog who cannot spend weeks on spreadsheets.

## What we need from you

Send us access to your current store as an admin, staff or collaborator user, or a data export if that is easier. Give us collaborator or staff access to your Shopify account. We never need your passwords. Tell us your domain provider, so we can plan the switch-over together, and list any pages you want to keep exactly as they are.
